status: candidates: Hongyu and the team pick the hero site; nothing here is final
rules: Do not open the pitch with Nov 11 or 1321 Flatbush Avenue.
Present records as what the public record shows, dated, with the source link. No owner, applicant or contractor names.
No blame and no 'would have prevented'. A site is a demo of what was knowable, not an accusation.
311 requests and DOB complaints are counted apart, never added: the same report can be in both.
Counts below are from live queries on 2026-11-14 and will change. Re-run the source query before the demo.

sites.label: 861 Park Avenue, Brooklyn (Bedford-Stuyvesant)
why_it_works: An active new building (50 dwelling units filed) on a vacant corner lot, wrapped by attached rowhouses built 1910 to 1931: the exact excavation-next-to-old-masonry profile ForeSite is built for.

The neighbors' own words are in the record: 7 'Excavation Undermining Adjacent Building' and 5 'Adjacent Buildings Not Protected' 311 requests between Feb and Sep 2026, plus 1 'Inadequate Support Shoring' in Jan 2026.

It shows a sequence, not a single event: shoring concern (Jan), undermining reports (Feb onward), 'Working Contrary To Stop Work Order' (May), more undermining reports (Aug). Good for the early-warning rules.
Neighbor-protection filings are on record (temporary needle-beam scaffolds and roof protection, Jul to Aug 2026), so the actions panel has real proof-needed items to point at.
No collapse or injury is publicly reported here, so the demo stays forward-looking and calm.

sites.label: 3728 Bronx Boulevard, Bronx (Williamsbridge)
why_it_works: A new 6-story, 28-unit building on a vacant lot, with separate foundation (Jun 2026), support-of-excavation (Sep 2026) and neighbor-overhead-protection (Sep 2026) filings: the work types map cleanly onto the actions by discipline.
9 'Adjacent Buildings Not Protected' 311 requests (Nov 2025 to Sep 2026) and 2 'Excavation Undermining Adjacent Building' (Nov 2025, Apr 2026).
2 'Working Contrary To Stop Work Order' requests in Jul 2026, a clean example of the stop-work-then-work-continued warning rule.
Touching lots mix older homes (built 1925 and 1928) with 2005 to 2006 rowhouses, which lets the similarity panel show both 'matches on' and 'differs on'.
A Bronx site keeps the demo from being only about Brooklyn.
